get.description: Every version of each policy, newest first. An action code with no row here needs no second signature, which is the state every action is in until somebody publishes one.
get.summary: List the approval policies governing this tenant

post.description: Never an edit. The previous open version is closed at the instant this one starts, so what an earlier approver was shown stays readable and the version snapshotted onto their request still means what it said.
post.summary: Publish the next version of an approval policy

get.description: An empty configuredScopes list is an unresolved action. Its missingPolicyMode states whether it currently proceeds on one signature or is refused until a policy is authored. A scoped row is not presented as tenant-wide coverage.
get.summary: Show registered approval actions and their configured scopes

post.description: Closes the version's window, which is the only way to retire a threshold: resolution takes the highest version whose window is open, so a superseding row cannot switch an earlier one off. This is how an operator says stop requiring approval, so it only applies to the version in force. Retroactive ends are refused, a closed version is never reopened — that is a new version — and a version scheduled to take effect later is refused too: cancelling it would leave the version it superseded closed with nothing to follow it, which turns the control off from the scheduled date onwards. To call off a scheduled change, publish the threshold you want as a new version.
post.summary: End-date a policy version

get.description: Oldest first, so the request closest to lapsing is the one on top. Lapsed requests are excluded whether or not the expiry sweep has reached them yet. The maker's free-text reason is deliberately not returned: it is unclassified prose about a named customer (ADR 0029), and the action's own console already holds the detail behind its own capability.
get.summary: List the requests waiting for a second signature

post.description: Refused unless the caller holds the capability the governing policy version named as the second signature, and refused outright if the caller is the person who raised the request. An approval lets the maker's identical resubmission proceed exactly once — executing under it moves the request to CONSUMED, so the next identical submission raises a new request needing a new signature. A decline blocks it with the reason given here. Both refusals and decisions are audited.
post.summary: Approve or decline a pending request

get.description: Reading audit is itself audited. The change document is not returned in a list; retrieving it is a separate, individually audited read.

get.description: The diff a settings or an order dispute is actually resolved with. Excluded from the list response on purpose (ADR 0027 §11.13): a change document can carry redacted structure that is still revealing in bulk, so retrieving it is a separate, individually audited read.

Either failure changes nothing.

post.description: ADR 0065: generalizes the endpoint above to a tenant that has no way to write a reference by hand. Accepts the new VALUE directly, verifies it (Telegram bot installations only, the same scoping rotateSecret already documents) before it is ever written anywhere, then writes it through the door under a freshly-minted reference and swaps the installation onto it. For every other provider type there is no harmless authenticated call to verify against, so the write proceeds and the installation is left last_connection_status = UNVERIFIED — connected, not silently claimed as confirmed, mirroring the Telegram-only scoping rationale rather than pretending a stronger guarantee.

post.description: Per-tenant, on the installation rather than a per-venue binding: the owner's own framing of the question was per tenant, and one Clopos installation is one brand. Defaults to true (the clerk decides) until set — an order sitting in PENDING awaiting a clerk is recoverable and visible, an auto-accepted one is already food, and CloposAdapter#exportOrder reads exactly this key.
post.summary: Set whether Clopos still needs a clerk's acceptance

get.summary: List the tenant's registered legal entities

post.description: Registered in DRAFT. A draft entity cannot be named as a seller until it is activated, so typing an INN never immediately puts it on a receipt.
post.summary: Register a company inside a tenant

get.summary: A location's fiscal-assignment history, most recent first
Get a legal entity

post.description: Only an ACTIVE entity may be named as a seller. Permitted from DRAFT or SUSPENDED.
post.summary: Activate a legal entity

post.description: Closes the location's currently open assignment, if any, at the new one's start date. Backdating is permitted; backdating over an existing assignment is refused.
post.summary: Assign a legal entity as a location's seller from a date

get.description: Live ones first.
get.summary: Every module the tenant has had

post.description: Omit templateId to use the template suited to the tenant's business type, or the platform's default when none suits it (ADR 0090). Set sampleMenu to create and publish a clearly marked sample menu for the tenant's first brand, so the platform can see the storefront answer before the tenant has authored anything (ADR 0099); omitting it is a no.
post.summary: Start an onboarding run

get.summary: The tenant's current onboarding run

get.description: The newest active template naming the tenant's business type, or the platform's default when none does. The console pre-selects it (ADR 0090).
get.summary: The template a new run would start under

get.description: Blocked steps are listed with the decision that would unblock them, so a tenant that is live without a check is visible rather than implied.
get.summary: One onboarding run with every step

post.description: Requires every required step to have completed, plus platform approval where a policy demands it. Activating twice produces one transition.
post.summary: Activate the tenant

post.description: The only way to stop a run: nothing else lets a tenant that started onboarding by mistake, or that will never fix a step, get free of it. Refused once the run has already reached ACTIVE or FAILED, and refused the same way for both — a failed run is repaired by resume (or superseded by a fresh run entirely), never abandoned by cancel, and an activated tenant is not un-activated by cancelling the run that activated it.
post.summary: Abandon a run that has not finished

post.description: Completed steps are never reset; a retry reconciles external work. Refused once the run has reached READY, ACTIVE or CANCELLED: nothing claims a step on a run the scheduler no longer drives, so reopening one there would report work that never happens.
post.summary: Reopen failed steps

post.description: Runs every read-only readiness check now, synchronously, against the tenant's current configuration rather than the run's persisted step status — so a tenant can see what activation would find before committing to a resume or an activate call. Nothing is written: a step's stored status only changes when the scheduler actually executes it. The activation smoke test is not included, because unlike every other check it is not a pure read. Use a fresh Idempotency-Key to see a fresh answer — replaying one returns the same recorded outcome, as ADR 0031 requires for every effectful request, even one with no state of its own to replay.
post.summary: Dry-run the tenant's current configuration

get.description: Omit brandId/locationId for the tenant-wide resolution; supply either to see what a specific brand or location actually resolves, including any override.
get.summary: The policy currently in force

post.description: Never edits a version in force. Orders already accepted keep the version they resolved (ADR 0030); this only changes what a new order resolves from now on.
post.summary: Publish the next version

get.description: Read with ORDER_READ rather than the manage capability, because the cancel dialog has to populate its list for every operator who can cancel an order and almost none of them may author one.
get.summary: The reasons of one kind

post.description: A cancellation reason decides the stock disposition, the liable party and the refund posture; none of the three has a safe default and all three are required. A completion reason names the fulfilment modes it is valid for, because without that «Самовывоз выполнен» lands on a delivery order and the courier SLA report quietly loses it.
post.summary: Register a reason

get.description: Closed and code-owned. Tenant registries drift into dozens of near-duplicates and that is contained rather than prevented: the category is what cross-tenant reporting groups by, and the tenant's own wording is only what the operator picks from.
get.summary: The platform categories a reason of this kind may carry

delete.description: Archived, never deleted. Outcomes recorded under it must still resolve, and the active-name uniqueness index frees the name for a replacement.

put.description: Outcomes already recorded keep the snapshot they were recorded with. That duplication is deliberate: renaming a reason next year must not rewrite last year's funnel.
put.summary: Rewrite a reason and bump its version

get.description: Queued, sent, opened, accepted, not needed, failed or expired, with when and why. The address is masked.
get.summary: The tenant owner's invitation

post.description: With a new link: one already sent stops working at once. For a tenant onboarded before invitations existed, sends the first one to the owner its onboarding linked. Refused once the owner has set up their account.
post.summary: Send the owner's invitation, or send it again

get.description: Exports whose outcome the platform could not establish. An empty list is the ordinary state; a growing one means a till or a network is unwell.
get.summary: Exports waiting on a decision

get.description: Provider orders that resemble this export. Resemblance is not identity: unless the provider echoed our own reference, none of these is proof.
get.summary: What the recovery read found

post.description: Side-effect free. It searches the provider and attaches what it found; it never re-sends the order.
post.summary: Read the provider to find out what happened

post.description: LANDED requires the provider order it landed as, because everything downstream — the fiscal write-back, the reconciliation — keys on it. ABSENT permits one further export attempt. ABANDON does not.
post.summary: Settle an export a person had to decide

post.description: Reads the provider, stages a snapshot, and produces a difference report. It stops there: nothing in this call changes a menu.
post.summary: Start a catalog import

post.description: Probes the provider with this restaurant's own credential. Capability varies per installation because the credential acts as a staff user the restaurant chose, so this is discovery and not a lookup.
post.summary: Rediscover what an installation can do

post.description: Refused for a dry run and for a run that is not REVIEW_REQUIRED. Plans every auto-applicable and approved difference, then executes what this build can — see PosApplyService for what that is today. An interrupted apply is picked up with resume, not by calling this again.
post.summary: Execute every eligible item an approved run produces

get.description: Deterministic: re-running the comparison over the same snapshot produces this list again, in this order.
get.summary: The difference report

post.description: A run interrupted before REVIEW_REQUIRED cannot resume mid-fetch -- the first provider offers no incremental read -- so this asks for a fresh PosSyncRequested run instead. A run interrupted mid-apply resumes exactly that: executing whatever apply item is still PLANNED, never re-applying one already APPLIED.
post.summary: Continue whatever this run's own interruption points left behind

post.description: Only a difference the engine recommended REVIEW accepts a decision. APPROVED means the provider's version becomes HorecaOS's, subject to what apply can actually execute; REJECTED and DEFERRED never do.
post.summary: Decide one difference recommended for review

post.description: Requires the global platform-admin role. Only a SUSPENDED tenant can be reactivated. Best-effort re-enables the tenant's Keycloak organization to match.
post.summary: Reactivate a suspended tenant

get.description: The eight tenant-visible PlatformRole bundles (staff-and-access.md §5 "Должности"), each with its capability codes. platform-admin and platform-support are never included. Tenant-defined roles are not yet supported (ADR 0025's deferred item) and so are not yet in this list.
get.summary: List the platform-defined jobs a tenant may see

get.description: Archived channels are listed because a historical order still renders through one; the status says whether a new cart may use it.
get.summary: List a tenant's sales channels, archived ones included

post.description: The system type comes from a closed, code-owned list. A tenant may run several channels of one type — Uzum Tezkor and Yandex Eda are both AGGREGATOR and must differ in price plane, payment mix, and reporting.
post.summary: Register a sales channel

post.description: Channels archive and never delete. Every order carries its channel forever, and a deleted row makes that order unattributable in every report.
post.summary: Archive a channel

put.description: Dine-in is a mode here and never a channel: a QR-table order and a waiter-entered order are both DINE_IN on different channels.
put.summary: Replace the channel's fulfilment-mode matrix

put.description: A location absent from the set is not served by the channel; the resolver returns CHANNEL_NOT_ENABLED rather than falling through to hours.
put.summary: Replace the set of locations selling on this channel

get.summary: The channel's payment, fulfilment, and location matrices

put.description: Whole matrix, never per cell: a matrix edited cell by cell from two tabs produces a combination neither operator chose.
put.summary: Replace the channel's payment-method matrix

post.description: Parses the export and reports, per row, what it would do (or, when dryRun=false, what it did): a matched or newly created customer account, a bound Telegram chat, an imported consent decision — or a rejection with a reason. Idempotent: importing the same file twice writes nothing new for a row already imported.
post.summary: Import a SendPulse contact export

get.description: The same report the run's own POST response returned, re-readable afterward without re-parsing the file.
get.summary: Re-read a past import run's report

get.description: Newest month first, void ones included.
get.summary: Every statement the tenant has been issued

get.description: Computed each time from the plan in force, the modules live during the month and the metered usage. Allowed for the month in progress.
get.summary: What a month would be billed if it were issued now
One issued statement with its lines

get.description: For the accounting system an invoice is made in. Amounts are integer minor units of the statement's currency.
get.summary: One issued statement as CSV
The tenant's live subscription
A tenant's support sessions, newest first

post.description: Confers a support-only role on the caller for this tenant until the session ends: between 15 minutes and 4 hours, never longer. VIEW looks; ASSIST also does the order-floor acts a location manager could. The reason is shown to the tenant and kept in their audit log.
post.summary: Open a support session into a tenant

post.description: Revokes the grant it conferred. Your own session, or anyone's if you are a platform administrator. Ending one that already ended changes nothing.
post.summary: End a support session now

post.description: Requires the global platform-admin role. Narrows every capability the tenant's people hold to a rationed read-only subset (ADR 0078) and best-effort disables the tenant's Keycloak organization so an operator reading Keycloak sees a matching state (ADR 0009) -- the flag is not itself an authentication control.
post.summary: Suspend a tenant

post.description: PENDING withholds it from sending until the answer is recorded; APPROVED needs the provider's reference and REJECTED what it objected to. NOT_REQUIRED sends as before.
post.summary: Record where an SMS wording stands with its gateway

get.description: Measured and adjusted quantities stay apart. A single consumed total cannot answer how much of a figure a person decided, and that is the first question asked about a disputed one.
get.summary: Metered usage per key and period

get.description: Filter by provider, or to calls whose signature did not check out — someone probing, or a key rotation one side missed.
get.summary: Payment providers' calls to HorecaOS, newest first

get.description: A counted key takes a limit and a feature takes on or off; a key not listed here is refused.
get.summary: The entitlement keys a plan version or override may name

get.description: The authoring view: each draft names who drafted it, because the person who activates it must be somebody else.
get.summary: Every module, drafts and retired ones included

post.description: The price is integer minor units of its currency per billing unit. The entitlements it names must be features; a module never raises a counted limit.
post.summary: Draft a module

post.description: Irreversible: its terms become immutable at the database. Refused when the approver drafted it.
post.summary: Put a module on sale

post.description: Tenants that have it keep it, and keep being billed for it, until it is ended for them.
post.summary: Stop selling a module

post.description: Irreversible: the version and its entitlements become immutable at the database. Refused when the approver is the version's author.
post.summary: Make a plan version live

get.description: The authoring view. Each draft names its author, because the person who activates it must be somebody else. The price list tenants read stays live versions only.
get.summary: Every plan with every version, drafts included

post.summary: Register a plan

post.description: Always a new version, never an edit. The price is integer minor units of the version's currency; for UZS a minor unit is one whole som.
post.summary: Draft a new version of a plan

post.description: Time-bounded is not optional. An open-ended override is a plan change made without changing the plan, and it outlives everyone who remembers why it was granted.
post.summary: Grant a time-bounded entitlement override

post.description: A quantity is required exactly when the module is billed per unit. Its features switch on while the tenant's subscription is in force.
post.summary: Give a tenant a module

post.description: Its features switch off now; the month it ended in still bills it.
post.summary: End a tenant's module

post.description: Only for a month that has ended, and only one standing statement per month: void the one that is wrong, then issue again.
post.summary: Issue a month's statement

post.description: It stays on record as void; the month is free to issue again.
post.summary: Void an issued statement

post.description: Suspension degrades what may be added and deletes nothing. The expected version is required, so two operators deciding at once settle at one outcome.
post.summary: Move a subscription's status

post.description: Manual assignment. ADR 0021's first slice does not automate recurring billing, and an operator's name against a subscription is an honest record of that rather than a placeholder.
post.summary: Put a tenant on a plan version

post.description: The only way a consumed figure ever changes. The movements that produced the original number stay exactly as they were recorded, which is what makes the correction defensible rather than merely applied.
post.summary: Correct a metered figure with a signed adjustment

post.description: Returns the periods whose cached figure disagreed, which should be empty. A non-empty answer is the alert an aggregate cache exists to make possible; a counter updated in place could never produce one.
post.summary: Recompute every cached total from the ledger

post.description: Completing is refused while any scope the program opened is short of RETIRED: a completed program reads as "this estate is off the legacy system", and saying that while a capability still has a legacy writer is what gets an old database decommissioned with live traffic on it.

post.description: A new run of a type that already has a live one is refused rather than queued, and the refusal names the run that is already going.
post.summary: Start a run over a scope

post.description: PAUSED is a decision somebody made and BLOCKED_RECONCILIATION is one evidence forced. The operator resuming it needs to know which.
post.summary: Pause a scope, or block it on reconciliation

post.description: TARGET_OWNED is not reachable here. Taking target ownership goes through the cutover endpoint, which records who approved it and on what evidence before the write mode moves.
post.summary: Advance a scope to its next state

post.description: Refused if the version is already signed. A second signature over the same words says nothing new, and replacing the first would lose who actually decided; a changed definition is a new version instead.
